field_legend.reference: where the art bible fixes this sprite: the section and rule that decide its look, and the craft recipe that decides its cell
field_legend.palette_roles: the entries it may spend, by role, and the scene sprite palette that carries them; a colour outside this list is a defect, not a choice

field_legend.defect: what is specifically wrong, named, with the count that shows it
field_legend.check: the command that decides the row, and what passing means
field_legend.status: queued, redrawn, done, queued_by_eye or retired
field_legend.measured_source: the authored file this row measures, its sidecar, its sha256, and the ruling that put it there
field_legend.ghost_before: the numbers this row used to carry, measured on a game/art copy that is now deleted; kept for the record, never to be read as evidence about what ships

priority_legend.P0: the sprite is wrong in a way the demo shows every second (off the PPU palette, impossible frame size, or missing)
priority_legend.P1: the sprite is palette legal but says the wrong thing (a flag colour where the reading needs a word, or an old identity)
priority_legend.P2: cosmetic, fix when the lane is idle

q_for_gamedev: Q1 RULE 0 point 2 against spec 14: is a 2 luminance row gap between body and ground meant to apply to a wordmark? Spec 14-8bit-look fixes the logo as weathered stone letters with a 1 px dark outline, and gamedev's scene file gives the wordmark exactly $0F, $00 and $28. On the title's own ground no body colour can satisfy both the 2 row gap (needs row 2 or 3) and the white blob rule (a pale body on the $12 sky at 0.39 luminance is refused), so the shipped sheet fails the same 6 pairs. If the wordmark is in scope for RULE 0 point 2, the drawing has to lose the stone body, which is a spec change; if it is out of scope, palette_synergy needs a way to judge a layer taller than one tile row that is drawn over the sky.

Q2 which sheet ships: this drawing adds spec 14's gold inlay on the foot row of every capital and the crack through the O, at 224x64 in the same three entries. ruling.q1_scope: Out of scope for a tiled layer. RULE 0 point 2's own subject is a character sprite that stands on something; the row gap and the white blob test are asked of characters and props. A layer is held to R1b overlay_contrast (3:1 with ink or body on every ground colour under it), which is now implemented in tools/palette_synergy.py on the same 16x32 size test the tool already used to skip the 3 colour sprite rule for a layer, and the ART-BIBLE carries the clause under point 2. Measured today: PASS, 0 failing pairs, every frame reading 'tiled layer so R1b'.
ground_ruling.why: the 6 pairs above are cf3d43a's per-8x8-tile R6 reading a 24 px wide sky element as a figure and asking the figure separation test (R1 body_ground, R2 same_hue_row, R3 white_blob) of a thing that stands on nothing. That reading is wrong on the facts, not only stale on the tool. The test that fits a sky element is R1b overlay_contrast, which asks that the ink OR the body clear 3:1 on every ground colour under it, and the cloud clears it on every one: on the sky $11 its body $20 reads 4.34:1, on the grey $00 it reads 3.93:1, and on the 5 white pixels its body is the ground colour at 1.00:1 while its ink $00 clears 3.93:1, which is what the or is for. The 5 white pixels in the crop (measured at 19,5 to 21,6 and 20,4 of the crop, 12 in the sky strip's own rows 80 to 95, and 0 in the parallax cloud layer) are the sky strip's own distant cloud tops, so a white crown over them is a cloud over a cloud, scenery meeting scenery, not a blob that has lost its edge. A figure test on that pair would fail it for sharing sky material with the sky.

If the cloud is ever re-declared a figure the 6 pairs return with the declaration and the third-entry decision is live again.
ground_ruling.q2_answer: Q2 closes. The row's palette_roles above stay as the legal set (the entries a cloud MAY spend on this band), and palette_roles_check records that the sheet can spend only $00 and $20 on the band as it stands. gamedev_ruling.q1: The exhaust puff is a TILED LAYER. game/sprites_src/title/spr_title_exhaust.json carries "layer": true, written by the generator (tools/art/make_title_car.py, LAYER_SHEETS), and its four fade twins inherit it through tools/pp_intro_art.py's fade_sidecar.
gamedev_ruling.why: The figure instrument presumes one ground and the puff has four. Swept over 1200 scroll steps from output/title_world_manifest.json, the 16x16 window at the game's placement (76, 207) holds $0F black 72.7 percent, $0B green 15.4, $0C teal 6.0, $20 white 5.9, all four in every frame, and the ends are luminance rows 0 and 2. A body clearing 3:1 on $0B (luma 0.0698) needs 0.31 or more; one clearing 3:1 on $20 (0.9387) needs 0.30 or less; the window is empty, and the row gap cannot help because no entry is two rows from both rows 0 and 2. Under R1b the pair passes on all four grounds: body $20 at 19.77:1 on $0F, 8.25:1 on $0B, 10.55:1 on $0C, and ink $0C at 10.55:1 on $20.
gamedev_ruling.q2_composer_order: The ordering is intended, not an accident. pp_title.gml's draw event draws the seven night layers first (line 488, title_L7_fg among them), then the sign, the cone, the car (line 491), the cloud, the logo, and inside pp_title_draw_car the exhaust is drawn before the car body. compose_title_preview.py pastes in the same order. The black under the puff is the road band's own tarmac, spent as bg3's shared backdrop $0F, and the sweep above is the evidence: the window's four entries are the road strip's.
gamedev_ruling.consequence_entries: The body moved from the redraw's $10 to $20, because the puff sits in screen bands 12 and 13 and the band plan gives those bg3 ($0C $0B $20). tools/art/title_bands.py flattens a $10 body to $20 on the way to the tree (measured: 118 pixels move), so the generator now draws the shipping pair and output/redraws is drawn in it too.

gamedev_ruling.ruling: Q1. The three entry sheet stands and tests/test_make_characters_v2.py is re-expressed for a three entry sheet.
why: Q2 is illegal on our own rules, not merely worse. A 16 x 16 cell spends ONE sprite palette of three (ART-BIBLE RULE 0 point 3, hardware rule 16), so four entries needs a second sprite palette on every scanline: that is the measured defect card t_bd5cfad5 removed, and palette_synergy reported 4 failing pairs on every one of the 8 frames before the redraw.

The four colour floor was never a gamedev spec. SPRITE-CRAFT 8.5 holds four numbers: the lightest share, zero dark free rows, at least 3 vertical dark runs in the body block, and at least 8 interior dark pixels. The test implemented three of them, invented a floor of four colours that no document carries, and skipped check 3.

The 30 percent ceiling in 8.5 was written for a sheet where a fourth entry could shade the cloth. On a three entry sheet the light tone carries the jumper and the face, so the ceiling moves to 8.5's own blob line of 45 percent, and the dark share floor of 30 percent plus check 3 take over the work the ceiling was doing.
